reasoning: The existing skill already covers identifying the requested target and preserving its scope, so those rules need no duplication. Both patches identify distinct gaps: choosing one directly supported label for a singular clue, and recognizing a clearly implied shared attribute in a bare list. Combine them in one append edit to avoid targeting the same location twice.

edits.content: When a clue requests one singular role or entity but context offers alternative labels, choose the single label most directly defined by the clue; do not return an “or” list unless alternatives are requested. When a prompt consists only of a list of two or more names or entities, treat it as an implicit request for a shared attribute only if context clearly supports one (for example, a common jurisdiction or affiliation). Give that shared attribute rather than a generic summary of the entities' relationship; if no single shared attribute is clearly intended, do not guess.
